summary: The purpose of this Motion is to request the application of permanent underspending from the Capital Budget for Economic Development and Culture to an urgent new project at the Toronto Centre for the Arts. The Toronto Centre for the Arts, built in 1993, requires a Building Condition Assessment to aid in future capital planning. To date, a Building Condition Assessment has not been done at this facility. The reallocation of this funding at this time will fulfil this need on a time line that will allow consideration of the resulting report as part of the 2019 Capital Budget process. Funding is available for this project through savings on roofing work at the St. Lawrence Centre for the Arts. All the planned 2018 roofing work at St. Lawrence Centre for the Arts will be completed by October 1, 2018. Significant savings will be achieved because this work was contracted though an amendment to the June 17, 2017 award to Semple Gooder through which: - Semple Gooder agreed to hold their original price. - No re-tendering was required (saving time/expense for staff and bidders, eliminating risk related to unknown contractor and likely escalation to 2019 prices). - Re-mobilization costs were not incurred, which were included in the original budget provision, resulting in an estimated savings of $160,000. decided: City Council on April 24, 25, 26 and 27, 2018, adopted the following: 1. City Council reduce the 2018 "St. Lawrence Centre Roof" capital project (CAC119-01) in the Capital Budget for Economic Development and Culture by $75,000, funded by capital from current, and transfer this funding to a new 2018 project in the Capital Budget for Economic Development and Culture for the Toronto Centre for Arts Building Condition Assessment with a project cost of $75,000.
